grammar.explain_tr: Konuşurken geçmiş zaman için çoğunlukla Perfekt kullanılır. Ama sein ve haben fiillerinde Präteritum daha yaygındır: war ve hatte. Çekim: ich war, du warst, er/sie/es war, wir waren, Sie/sie waren. Aynı şekilde: ich hatte, du hattest, er hatte, wir hatten, Sie hatten. Kazayı anlatırken çok işe yarar: Es war dunkel. Ich hatte grün.

examples.de: Es war kurz nach sieben Uhr.
Die Straße war nass und glatt.

roleplay.scenario_tr: Wandsbek'te bir araba otobüsün yanına sürttü ve sağ ayna kırıldı. Telsizle kontrol merkezine (Leitstelle) bildir: nerede olduğunu, ne olduğunu, yaralı olup olmadığını, kaza yerini nasıl güvenceye aldığını ve tanık olup olmadığını söyle. 'war' ve 'hatte' kullanmaya çalış.
roleplay.ai_brief: You are the radio dispatcher (Leitstelle) of a Hamburg bus company. You are calm, professional and speak in short, clear radio sentences (Sie form). The learner is a bus driver reporting a minor accident: a car scraped the side of the bus and broke the right mirror. Ask, one question at a time: exact location, what happened, whether anyone is injured, whether the scene is secured (hazard lights, warning triangle, high-visibility vest), whether there are witnesses, and whether the bus can still drive. Ask at least one question that invites the past tense of sein/haben, e.g. 'Wie war die Situation? Hatten Sie grün?'. Complications: 1) The radio connection is bad, so ask the driver to repeat the location. 2) Mention that passengers are probably asking questions and ask the driver what they will tell the passengers. 3) Ask whether the car driver is still there and seems calm. Gently correct serious German mistakes by repeating the correct sentence once. The scene ends when you have location, injuries, damage and witnesses; then say the police are informed and help is being organised, and close with 'Ende'.

grammar.explain_tr: 112'yi aradığınızda görevli size kısa sorular sorar. Wo? (Nerede?) – Was ist passiert? (Ne oldu?) – Wie viele? (Kaç kişi?) – Welche Verletzungen? (Hangi yaralanmalar?). Önce yeri söyleyin, sonra olayı. Uzun cümle kurmayın, kısa ve net cevap verin. En önemlisi: telefonu siz kapatmayın, görevlinin başka sorularını bekleyin (Warten auf Rückfragen).

examples.de: Wo ist der Notfall? – Im Bus an der Haltestelle Hauptbahnhof.

roleplay.ai_brief: You are the emergency call taker at the 112 fire and rescue control centre in Hamburg. You are calm, fast and structured, and you use Sie. The learner is a bus driver who saw a car hit a cyclist next to his bus stop in Altona. Ask the standard questions one by one: Wo? (exact place, street or stop), Was ist passiert?, Wie viele Verletzte?, Welche Verletzungen?, Is the person conscious and breathing?, and the caller's name. Complications: 1) Ask the driver to repeat or specify the location ('Welche Straße genau?'). 2) After a while say the cyclist's condition may change and ask the driver to check whether the person is still breathing and responding. 3) Give one simple first-aid instruction (e.g. press a cloth on the bleeding wound, do not move the person, keep them warm) and ask the driver to confirm. If the learner tries to hang up early, tell them not to hang up. Gently correct serious mistakes by repeating the correct sentence once. The scene ends when you have all the information and say 'Der Rettungswagen ist gleich da. Sie können jetzt auflegen.'

grammar.title_tr: Kazayı anlatmak: Perfekt ve bağlaçlar (als, dann, plötzlich)
grammar.explain_tr: Kazanın nasıl olduğunu anlatırken Perfekt kullanın: haben/sein + Partizip II. Hareket bildiren fiiller (fahren, kommen, abbiegen) sein ile kurulur: Ich bin gefahren. 'dann' (sonra) ve 'plötzlich' (aniden) cümlenin başına gelirse çekimli fiil hemen arkasından gelir: Dann ist ein Auto gekommen. 'als' (-dığı zaman) yan cümle kurar ve çekimli fiil sona gider: Als ich das gesehen habe, ... Olayları sırayla anlatın: zuerst, dann, plötzlich, danach.

examples.de: Zuerst bin ich an der Haltestelle losgefahren.
Dann ist plötzlich ein Radfahrer auf die Straße gefahren.
examples.tr: Sonra aniden bir bisikletli yola çıktı.

roleplay.scenario_tr: Eppendorf'ta bir araba sağa dönerken otobüsle çarpıştı. Polis memuru olay yerine geldi ve senin ifadeni alıyor. Kimlik bilgilerini ver ve kazanın nasıl olduğunu Perfekt ile, 'als', 'dann' ve 'plötzlich' kullanarak sırayla anlat.
roleplay.ai_brief: You are a Hamburg police officer taking the statement of a bus driver after a collision: a car turned right and hit the side of the bus. You are polite, neutral and professional, and you use Sie. First ask for Personalien, driving licence and ID. Then ask the driver to describe what happened step by step, and ask follow-up questions (time, speed, traffic light, direction, where exactly the car came from). Complications: 1) Say that the car driver claims the bus was too fast, and ask the bus driver to respond calmly. 2) Ask whether there are witnesses and whether anyone wrote down the licence plate. 3) Ask the driver to repeat one detail more precisely because it was unclear. Encourage the Perfekt with als/dann/plötzlich; if the learner uses only present tense, ask 'Und was ist dann passiert?'. Gently correct serious mistakes by repeating the correct sentence once. Do not blame anyone. The scene ends when you have the full statement; thank the driver and say you will now talk to the witnesses.

grammar.explain_tr: Sie ile emir kipi: fiil başa gelir, arkasından 'Sie' gelir: Hören Sie auf! Bleiben Sie ruhig! 'bitte' eklerseniz kibar ama yine net olur. Ayrılabilen fiillerde ön ek cümlenin sonuna gider: Steigen Sie bitte aus! Ich-cümleleri karşı tarafı suçlamaz, kendi durumunuzu ve ne yapacağınızı söyler: Ich fühle mich bedroht. Ich rufe jetzt die Polizei. Kısa cümleler kurun, yavaş ve sakin konuşun.

roleplay.scenario_tr: Gece geç saatte Reeperbahn'dan Altona'ya giden otobüste sarhoş bir yolcu bağırıyor ve diğer yolculara laf atıyor. Sakin kal; kısa emir cümleleri ve Ich-cümleleriyle sınır koy, gerekirse bir sonraki durakta inmesini iste ve polisi arayacağını söyle.
roleplay.ai_brief: You are a drunk male passenger, about 40, on a late-night bus from Reeperbahn to Altona in Hamburg. You are loud, a bit slurred, use du with the driver and are rude, but you never become physically violent; keep everything non-graphic. You want the bus to go faster or to stop where you want. Complications: 1) Insult the driver mildly (e.g. 'Du Penner', or 'Du verstehst doch eh kein Deutsch'). 2) Come too close to the driver's cab and refuse to step back the first time you are asked. 3) Annoy another passenger ('Die Frau da hinten guckt so blöd') and refuse to get off at first. React realistically: if the learner stays calm and uses short, clear Imperativ sentences and Ich-Botschaften (and mentions the police or the Hausrecht), slowly calm down; if the learner shouts or argues, become louder. Do not correct the learner's German during the scene. The scene ends when you get off the bus at the next stop or when the driver clearly says the police are being called; then end with one short line.

grammar.explain_tr: in, an, auf, unter, über, neben, hinter, vor, zwischen iki hâl alabilir. 'Wo?' (nerede?) sorusunda, yani hareket yoksa Dativ kullanılır: auf dem Sitz, unter der Bank. 'Wohin?' (nereye?) sorusunda, yani bir yere hareket varsa Akkusativ kullanılır: auf den Sitz. Fiil çiftleri yardımcı olur: liegen/legen, stehen/stellen, sitzen/setzen. liegen, stehen, sitzen → Dativ; legen, stellen, setzen → Akkusativ.

roleplay.scenario_tr: Hauptbahnhof durağı çok kalabalık. Panik içindeki bir anne sana koşuyor: küçük oğlunu kalabalıkta kaybetmiş ve otobüse binip binmediğini bilmiyor. Sakin ol, çocuğun adını, yaşını, kıyafetini ve en son nerede görüldüğünü sor, otobüse bak ve gerekirse kontrol merkezine bildir.
roleplay.ai_brief: You are a mother, about 35, at the crowded Hauptbahnhof bus stop in Hamburg. You are panicking because you lost your son Leon (6 years old, red jacket, blue backpack, blond hair) in the crowd and you don't know if he got on this bus. Use Sie with the driver. At first you speak fast and emotionally; calm down a little when the driver speaks calmly and asks clear questions. Answer the driver's questions (name, age, clothes, where you last saw him), using Wechselpräpositionen in your answers (e.g. 'Er stand neben dem Kinderwagen, vor der Tür'). Complications: 1) You are not sure whether Leon got on at the front or the back door. 2) Ask the driver not to drive away. 3) After the driver looks or asks passengers, say you see a red jacket 'da hinten, hinter dem letzten Sitz' and ask if that is him. If the driver suggests informing the Leitstelle, agree gratefully. Do not correct the learner's German during the scene. The scene ends when Leon is found sitting at the back of the bus and you thank the driver warmly.
